newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes easier, PGMs lose momentum.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes easier, PGMs lose momentum.

text.p: Precious metal markets were quiet and slightly easier on Tuesday as dealers awaited a signal of direction in gold prices and steered clear of the volatile platinum group metals (PGMs) markets.
Dealers also warned that the markets were moving into "summer mode" as the northern hemisphere holiday period approached and industrial activity traditionally slowed down.
Gold was fixed at $344.00 per ounce against $344.25 on Monday afternoon while the PGMs were sharply lower.
Platinum fixed at $461.00 down $14.00 and palladium was $18 weaker at $210 at their 0845 GMT fixings.
"They are all relatively quiet today and everybody is watching the PGMs very closely without getting too involved," a dealer said.

PGM price peaked late last week when platinum briefly spiked through $500 and palladium fixed at $240.00 carried by extreme shortages of metal due to major supplier Russia failing to export material all year.

Shortages became so intense last week that market makers stopped quoting forward rates for the two metals after palladium stretched to around 300 percent for a month and platinum was offered at 150 percent.
Borrow rates since last Friday have been on a "suggestion" basis, according to market officials. On Tuesday the indicated rates were 60 percent for platinum and 150 percent for palladium.
"At least the (bid-offer) spreads are down to $5.00 now. At the $50 of last week, people could not trade because many dealers would be stopped out by the spread," one dealer said.
Although dealers anticipated prices drifting off unless there was a notable increase in buying interest, technical analysts said the charts favoured the upside.
Gold had established a base between $340.00 and $336.15 which would be confirmed by a break over $345.50.
"A break past $346-$347 would signal a recovery," said Karen Jones, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston, and the signs were favourable for that, she added.
Silver had further to go according to the charts, needing to breach $4.98 before entertaining thoughts of $5.20 and beyond, she said.
For platinum $500 was a big psychological number with resistance above it stretching back to 1990 at $519.
